newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds rise on FRN spread cuts, lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds rise on FRN spread cuts, lower rates.

text.p: Greek floaters and coupon bonds posted impressive gains in late dealings, boosted by FRN spread cuts and the lower than expected yield to maturity on two-year zero coupon notes to be issued on January 20, dealers said.

"We are talking about the rally," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "All FRN and bond prices have skyrocketed on news of FRN spread cuts, the lower than expected rate on the two-year zero coupon T-note and lower T-bill rates."
The market expected the ministry to set the interest rate on the two-year zero-coupon T-note at 10.50 percent instead of the actual 10.30 percent.
The finance ministry also cut seven-, five- and three-year FRN spreads by 10 basis points to 1.30 percent, 0.80 percent and 0.30 percent respectively.
The ministry will auction seven-year floaters and three-year coupon bonds on January 20 with January 28 as settlement date.
It also reduced the benchmark 12-month T-bill rate to 11.10 percent from 11.20 percent and the six-and three-month T-bill rates by 20 basis points to 10 and 10.30 percent respectively.

The dealer said bond prices had advanced so much that offers had disappeared in some cases. "Those with large holdings of outstanding FRNs and coupon bonds realised huge capital gains today," said a senior dealer.
The climate of euphoria spilled over to the money markets, where depos eased 10 basis points across the spectrum along with forex forwards.

"Depos have eased 10 basis points although the Buba of the Balkans left its intervention rate in overnight funds unchanged at 12.40 percent," the senior dealer said. One-year implied forwards have dropped below 10 percent, he said.
The mark was quoted at 155.97/07 drachmas from Friday's 155.890 fix, the dollar at 250.26/36 drachmas from 248.150 and the Ecu at 303.29/39 from 303.320 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma has been hovering in the 303.20/70 range throughtout the day," said a senior dealer at a private bank.
